This is a full implementation pass, not a design/prototype/planning exercise.

Your task is to inspect the existing Haven repository, understand the current architecture, implement the entire specification below, integrate it with the existing application, migrate required existing functionality, remove superseded systems, test the result, and leave the repository in a releasable state.
Do not stop after producing plans, interfaces, placeholder services, mock implementations, TODOs, or partially connected UI.
Transform Haven into an application built around:
while preserving all existing user-facing functionality unless this specification explicitly removes or replaces it.
The result must be suitable for preparing Haven for release.
When implementation details conflict, use the following precedence:
2. UI behaviour/layout shown in the attached presentation/mockups.
3. Existing working Haven behaviour that is not explicitly replaced.
4. Existing architecture/conventions where compatible with the new design.
Do not preserve legacy architecture merely because it already exists if this specification explicitly replaces it.
However, do not delete useful functionality simply because its old implementation is being removed.
**Legacy implementation may be removed. User functionality must be migrated.**

For example, if Browse, Plan, Write, Tasks, model handling, actions, projects, or other features depend on a system being removed, migrate those features to the replacement architecture before deleting their old dependencies.

text: Consolidate duplicate implementations during this overhaul.
When Haven generates an app for use inside Haven, it should feel like a native part of Haven rather than an unrelated webpage embedded into it.

If the user explicitly asks Haven to reproduce a particular external visual style, Haven may customise the **content styling** of that generated experience, but common controls and Haven-hosted chrome must still use HavenUI unless the user explicitly instructs Haven to alter those controls too.
A request for custom styling of one generated app does **not** authorise a global HavenUI redesign.
Generated UI must not mutate global HavenUI resources simply to style one thread/app.

HavenUI work is complete only when:

- Magical UI styling code has been removed.
- Common controls use canonical HavenUI components.

- App accent colours work without creating separate themes.
- Generative UI uses the HavenUI component registry.
- Generated UI does not mutate global theme state.

- Mockups in the attached presentation are closely followed.

headingPath: 6.27 Mandatory HavenUI Rules for Future Development
text: The intended result is that HavenUI is fully adopted during this release pass and then remains stable, predictable, centrally controlled and visually consistent over the lifetime of Haven.
HavenUI must include a **centralised motion/animation system**.
Haven-owned UI should feel fluid and physically connected rather than behaving like a collection of controls that instantly teleport between states.
Animations are part of HavenUI and must therefore be:
- compatible with all four HavenUI colour modes
- inherited by generated internal UI wherever appropriate
Do not independently invent unrelated animation styles for individual screens.
When a visible HavenUI component changes position, it should normally animate from its previous position to its new position rather than instantly teleporting.
- expanding an app into the workspace
Movement should visibly glide between states.
Where technically practical, use layout-aware/shared-element transitions so the component appears to remain the same object while moving.
When components change size, the transition should be visibly animated.
- editors taking over more of the workspace
between their previous and new geometry.
Avoid instantly replacing one size with another where an animated transition is reasonable.
Components entering the current UI should normally **fade in** rather than instantly appearing.
Components being removed should normally **fade out** before disappearing.
Where appropriate, entry/exit animations may combine fading with subtle:
but animations should remain coherent with the HavenUI motion language rather than becoming excessive or distracting.
HavenUI components should smoothly animate suitable state changes.
Do not animate properties where doing so would reduce usability or create unnecessary visual noise.
Switching between major tabs or Apps uses a different transition rule.
When switching from one major Haven tab/App to another:
**Do not animate every individual child component independently.**
Instead, treat the outgoing and incoming App/screen as complete visual surfaces.
The transition must occur at the **whole-screen/App level**.
1. Current App/screen begins its exit transition.
2. The entire outgoing surface transitions/fades/moves out as one coherent unit.
3. The incoming App/screen transitions in as one coherent unit.
4. Its internal controls remain visually stable relative to each other.
This prevents switching Apps from looking like dozens of unrelated controls flying around the screen.
- Settings sections represented as major surfaces
The exact transition can follow the approved HavenUI motion design, but the **entire App/screen must transition rather than independently animating all of its child components**.
Generative UI must use HavenUI motion when changing the workspace.
the interface must visibly transition between those layouts.
- preserve visual continuity where the same component remains present
Do not destroy the existing layout and instantly render an unrelated replacement.
Where possible, Haven should understand which components persist between states and animate them to their new geometry.
For example, the existing chat bar may glide to a new position rather than disappearing and being recreated elsewhere.
When the layout changes because the available viewport changes, use animation where appropriate.
- controls reorganising as window width changes
However, avoid excessive animation during continuous window resizing.
- temporarily suppressed during rapid continuous resizing
and then used when settling into a new responsive layout state.
Performance and responsiveness take priority over attempting to animate every individual pixel of a live resize.
Animation values must be centrally defined within HavenUI.
Define reusable motion tokens for concepts such as:
- Instant/None where animation is intentionally inappropriate
Do not scatter arbitrary animation durations and easing curves throughout individual views.
Changing HavenUI's canonical movement behaviour must be possible from a small number of central definitions.
If the same logical component exists before and after a layout change, prefer animating that component between states rather than:
For example, if the Browser panel moves from beside Write into picture-in-picture, the Browser surface should visually move and resize into that position where technically practical.
Animations should feel polished rather than mechanical.
Use appropriate easing rather than constant linear movement for most interface transitions.
- arrive cleanly at its final position
- avoid exaggerated elastic behaviour unless explicitly part of the HavenUI motion design
Animations may use subtle squash/stretch or spring-like behaviour where appropriate, particularly when resizing or settling components, but they should remain professional and usable.
Animations should not make Haven feel slow.
- allow interaction as soon as practical
- avoid delaying important user actions solely for visual effect
- interrupt or retarget animations when the user performs another action
For example, if a sidebar is currently expanding and the user immediately collapses it, the animation should smoothly reverse/retarget rather than requiring the first animation to finish.
Generative UI transitions must be capable of handling rapid state changes safely.

If Haven begins moving components into one layout and the desired layout changes before the transition completes, the motion system should transition from the **current visual state** toward the new target state where technically practical.
Fancy animation must not come at the cost of an unusable interface.

If an expensive effect cannot run smoothly on a supported device, gracefully reduce the complexity of the effect while preserving the general motion/transition rather than allowing severe frame drops.
Respect the operating system's reduced-motion/accessibility preference where available.
- preserve enough transition feedback for state changes to remain understandable
Reduced motion should not disable essential state feedback.
Internal apps generated by Haven must use the HavenUI motion system.
Generated code should reference HavenUI motion primitives/tokens rather than inventing its own animation framework.

unless the user explicitly requests a specialised animation for that generated experience.

- App/tab switches animate as complete surfaces

**The intended result is that HavenUI feels like a fluid, living workspace: components glide, resize and fade naturally as the workspace changes, while major App/tab changes transition as coherent complete surfaces.**

text: ## 6.29 Floating Activities and Detached HavenUI Surfaces

headingPath: 6.29 Floating Activities and Detached HavenUI Surfaces
text: HavenUI must be architected from this release onward to support **Floating Activities**.

headingPath: 6.29 Floating Activities and Detached HavenUI Surfaces
text: A Floating Activity is a Haven-owned UI surface that can appear separately from the normal main Haven workspace while still using the same HavenUI design system.

headingPath: 6.29 Floating Activities and Detached HavenUI Surfaces
text: The complete end-user Floating Activities product experience does not need to be introduced in this release unless required elsewhere by this specification, but **the reusable HavenUI floating architecture and a representative detached runtime host must be implemented and validated in this pass** so future Floating Activities can be added without redesigning or replacing the UI system.

headingPath: 6.29 Floating Activities and Detached HavenUI Surfaces
text: This requirement includes a **real generic Android Floating Activity host/provider in this release**, not merely a shared interface or desktop-only implementation. The Android host must be capable of presenting supported HavenUI floating content through an Android-appropriate floating/overlay mechanism when the required OS capability/permission exists, and it must be runtime-validated independently of any one product feature. Do not couple the generic Android Floating Activity implementation to Voice or any other single consumer.

text: ## 7.8 Model Residency, Always Loaded and Fast-Wake Behaviour

headingPath: 7.8 Model Residency, Always Loaded and Fast-Wake Behaviour
text: Local models can have substantial cold-start/wake latency. Haven must therefore provide an explicit **model residency/lifecycle setting** that lets the user choose how the active local model runtime behaves when the main Haven UI is closed.

headingPath: 7.8 Model Residency, Always Loaded and Fast-Wake Behaviour
text: At minimum support user-facing semantics equivalent to:

headingPath: 7.8 Model Residency, Always Loaded and Fast-Wake Behaviour
text: 1. **Unload when Haven closes** — close/swipe away the ordinary Haven UI and release the active local model/runtime according to the configured backend policy. This minimises background RAM/VRAM/CPU/GPU use but means a later local-model request may require a cold start.

headingPath: 7.8 Model Residency, Always Loaded and Fast-Wake Behaviour
text: 2. **Always Loaded / Keep Haven Models Ready** — keep the configured resident local model/runtime alive after the ordinary Haven UI is closed or swiped away so reopening Haven, Voice/background work and other authorised Haven background tasks can use it without paying the full model wake/load cost again.

headingPath: 7.8 Model Residency, Always Loaded and Fast-Wake Behaviour
text: The exact labels may follow the mockups, but the behaviour must be clear. Do not implement **Always Loaded** as merely "stay loaded while the window is minimised." A normal UI close/swipe-away must leave the configured resident runtime alive where the operating system permits.

Generated UI supplements conversation; it must not eliminate it. The user must remain able to type natural-language requests, ask what the UI means, refer to selections, reject structured options, or provide an unlisted alternative.
If a generated choice offers A/B/C, the user may still type "None of those — use D." The agent must remain capable of adapting.
The active agent must receive/retrieve enough structured current-state information to resolve contextual references such as:
- the red point, where the semantic selected/identified point is available
Do not rely on screenshot/vision interpretation of Haven's own UI when the runtime already has a structured identity/selection/state representation.
If the user directly changes meaningful UI state, subsequent agent reasoning must use the new authoritative state.
The user may ask the agent to modify the generated interface itself.
- "Put the graph next to the quiz."
Map these to structured incremental GenUI operations where possible and preserve unrelated state.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: ## 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: Haven Voice must support **Haven-provided and user-created Voice Modes**.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: The user-facing term **Voice Mode** is permitted here because it describes a configuration/profile inside Haven's **Voice subsystem** (and the Call App where Call is the current owning App). It does **not** reintroduce the legacy top-level Haven Mode architecture replaced by Apps in Section 74, and Codex must not create a new Call App solely to provide a home for Voice Modes if the current repository uses a different Voice owner.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: Internally, prefer a scoped concept such as a Voice Profile/Voice Experience contract rather than making new product architecture depend on legacy `Mode`, `HavenMode`, `ModeId`, or a global Mode registry.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: A Voice Mode defines how Haven should listen, interpret, respond, use Apps/templates, and invoke permitted actions during a particular real-time voice context.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: Haven must provide first-party Voice Modes and allow users to create their own reusable Voice Modes through the same broad architecture.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: A Voice Mode **must expose structured metadata/configuration where relevant**, including concepts such as:

75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: Do not implement first-party Voice Modes as unrelated bespoke audio pipelines when they can share the same trusted Voice runtime, Action/Event Router, capability system, App services and permission architecture.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: Provide a first-party **Lesson Voice Mode** intended to follow a real lesson/class session continuously in real time and orchestrate the appropriate Haven Apps, templates, state and actions as the lesson changes.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: Lesson Voice Mode must behave as a live lesson companion rather than merely a passive transcription/summary feature. It must maintain a structured understanding of the current lesson state and react to meaningful transitions such as:

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - web/classroom activity (for example Kahoot or Google Classroom)

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: The exact internal state model may differ, but Haven **must preserve continuity across these phases** instead of treating each detected instruction as an unrelated event.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: A representative flow must support behaviour equivalent to:

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 1. Teacher says something such as: **"Whiteboards out, starter task."**

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 2. Haven recognises that the lesson has entered a starter/whiteboard activity.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 3. Haven presents or reuses an appropriate HavenUI Whiteboard / learning surface inside the current conversation/Teach workspace.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 4. If the teacher verbally states the starter questions and Haven can reliably identify/finalise them, Haven **must populate them into the active Whiteboard** as they are finalised. It may wait for sufficient speech finalisation/context rather than committing unstable interim recognition.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 5. If the teacher instead says something such as **"The starter questions are on the board"**, Haven must not invent the questions. It **must present or reuse a blank Whiteboard immediately** so the user can work manually, while any separately authorised vision path may populate visible questions only when they are actually observed.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 6. If an authorised visual input is available and the user chooses/has configured it for the lesson, Haven may inspect the board/screen and populate the task from the visible content through the normal image-inspection/vision capability.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 7. The user's written answers/work remain associated with the specific question/task identities so later marking can refer to the real work rather than guessing from rendered pixels.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: The Whiteboard must use the existing HavenUI/template architecture and structured GenUI state/events. Do not build a Voice-only drawing surface disconnected from Teach/GenUI.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: When the likely teacher begins reviewing answers, Haven must recognise the transition into an answer-review/marking phase and connect spoken marking guidance to the user's existing lesson work.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 1. The user's starter answers remain visible/stored in the active lesson state.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 2. The teacher begins saying the correct answers or working through them.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 3. Haven associates each announced answer/explanation with the corresponding question where confidence is sufficient.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 4. Haven compares the teacher's answer/marking guidance with the user's real response.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 5. Haven updates the Whiteboard/Teach state incrementally with appropriate marking, corrections, explanations or confidence indicators.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: 6. The resulting confirmed learning outcome may feed Teach progress/revision state without storing the entire classroom transcript.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: Do not wait until the lesson ends to mark work that can be reliably marked in real time.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: Do not falsely mark work when Haven cannot confidently determine:

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - what the teacher's final answer actually was

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - which user response belongs to that question

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - whether the teacher is giving an example, misconception or final marking guidance

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: In ambiguous cases, preserve the work and wait for more context or surface a low-friction clarification rather than confidently writing an incorrect mark.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: Lesson Voice Mode may identify a likely error in spoken teaching/marking when the contradiction is **provable or supported with sufficiently strong evidence**.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - deterministic arithmetic/algebra contradicting the announced answer

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - the teacher immediately misspeaks and gives a result inconsistent with their own working

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - an authoritative/local course reference clearly contradicts a factual claim

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: Do not treat model confidence alone as proof that the teacher is wrong.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: Where the teacher appears provably wrong, Haven should normally flag the discrepancy discreetly in the user's lesson UI and explain the basis. It must not automatically interrupt or audibly challenge the teacher unless the user has explicitly configured that behaviour.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: For uncertain or current factual claims, use appropriate trusted references/research when available or label the issue as uncertain rather than asserting correction.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: When the lesson moves from a task/marking phase into teacher explanation or taught content, Haven must be able to transition the workspace into an appropriate **Write/Notes** experience while preserving the active lesson context.

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: The user **must be able to choose/configure** at least two broad note-taking behaviours:

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - the user writes their own notes in Write

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - Haven follows the explanation in real time

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - Haven can point out likely factual mistakes in the user's notes

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - Haven can flag important taught content that appears to have been omitted

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - Haven can suggest concise corrections/additions without rewriting everything unnecessarily

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - Haven writes structured notes from the taught content in real time or near-real time

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - remove filler/rambling/repetition that does not improve the notes

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - preserve important definitions, explanations, examples, methods, caveats and teacher emphasis

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - organise the notes into useful headings/bullets/structures rather than producing a verbatim transcript

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: - avoid inventing details that were not taught merely to make the notes look complete

headingPath: 75.5 Haven Voice Modes / Voice Interaction Profiles
text: This must use the real Write document model. Voice must not maintain a disconnected private notes buffer presented as though it were Write.

Haven must include a **real optional Android system launcher/homescreen experience**, referred to here as **Haven Home**. This is a first-class Haven-owned surface and is distinct from the obsolete Old-Haven/New-Haven startup chooser removed by Clause 4.2.

The user must be able to select Haven Home through Android's normal launcher/default-home mechanisms. When selected, pressing the system Home action must return to the Haven Home workspace rather than merely opening an ordinary Haven Activity that imitates a launcher.
Haven Home must use **HavenUI** and support the **Generative UI, App, Template, Action/Event Router and Capability Registry architecture** rather than creating a second independent UI/action system.

Haven Home is incomplete if it is only a wallpaper, static app grid or AI demo. Codex must treat it as a production launcher with the ordinary core workflows and quality-of-life capabilities users reasonably expect from mature Android launchers in the Nova Launcher/Lawnchair class, while following Haven's own visual design rather than cloning another product.
At minimum the Success Rubric must enumerate, implement and runtime-test a launcher feature-completeness contract covering applicable capabilities such as:
- add/remove/reorder pages and choose/default the primary page where appropriate
- drag/drop repositioning with sensible grid/snap behaviour
- configurable dock/favourites area where used by the mockups
- complete app drawer with launchable installed apps
- Android application shortcuts/long-press actions where exposed by the platform
- Android app widgets, including add/place/resize/remove and proper widget-host lifecycle
- Haven/GenUI widgets and generated interactive surfaces
- icon labels, adaptive icons and common icon/customisation behaviour appropriate to the supported Android APIs
- grid/icon-size/layout controls where defined by the mockups/settings
- notification dots/badges where supported and authorised
- long-press/context actions such as App Info, remove-from-home, uninstall/request-uninstall where platform rules allow, and other expected item actions
- page/app/folder drag-and-drop with clear insertion/drop feedback
- undo/recovery for accidental home-layout edits where practical
- launcher settings and sensible reset/restore behaviour
- persistent layout/state across app restarts and device reboots
- accessibility, keyboard/navigation support where applicable, readable focus/selection state and large-enough touch targets
- performance sufficient for ordinary launcher use without obvious jank or unnecessary model invocation
Codex must inspect the existing launcher implementation, if any, before replacing it and preserve useful working behaviour. A visually polished but functionally incomplete launcher does not pass.
Haven Home must feel like Haven, not like a conventional launcher with an unrelated AI panel glued on top.

All Haven-owned launcher chrome, edit controls, generated pages, widgets, menus, sheets, search surfaces, folders and settings must follow HavenUI, including the active colour mode, accents, motion, accessibility and responsive rules. Android application icons/widgets may of course retain their own external visual content inside the Haven-owned host surface.
Generative UI must be able to compose and modify homescreen pages using the same trusted declarative/template architecture as the rest of Haven. A generated homescreen page may combine:
- Haven Apps or embeddable App surfaces
Generated content must remain editable/rearrangeable by the user and must survive subsequent agent updates without the agent constantly undoing deliberate manual layout choices.
The architecture must support requests equivalent to:
> "Make me a homescreen page with a button that generates a random YouTube Music set list and a Play button."

A valid implementation may generate a HavenUI page containing the required controls/state, but the buttons must not be fake. The semantic action path must use the normal Action/Event Router and the authorised YouTube Music/media/external-App capability/integration path that is actually available.
2. the generated control emits a structured semantic event
3. Haven generates/selects the set list using the appropriate deterministic/agent logic
4. the page visibly updates with the resulting tracks/metadata
6. Haven routes playback through the real authorised media/external integration
7. actual success/failure/playback state returns to the same homescreen surface
If the relevant account/integration/capability is unavailable, the page must show that honestly and offer the appropriate connection/recovery path rather than simulating playback.
This is an example of the architecture, not a hard-coded YouTube-Music-only launcher subsystem.
Haven's active agent must be able to inspect and modify the launcher through structured semantic actions and stable launcher-object identities.
Representative user requests must be supportable through real production paths, for example:
- "Put all my college apps in a folder."
- "Move this widget to the next page."
The agent must use structured page/item/folder/widget IDs and the launcher state model rather than screen-coordinate automation against Haven's own launcher.

Launcher changes should be visibly animated/applied in place according to the GenUI live-manipulation principle. The user must see items move, groups form, widgets resize or pages appear rather than receiving only a chat message saying the layout changed.

Consequential actions still obey normal permissions. Rearranging Haven-owned launcher layout is generally a local App-owned action; launching apps, sending media commands, controlling devices, uninstalling applications or invoking external services must use the appropriate capability/permission path.

Natural-language launcher requests that modify state must route through the same structured action/event architecture as equivalent requests in Chat. The launcher must not maintain a parallel agent command language.
Generated launcher pages are not a permission bypass.
- external app/media/device actions use normal capabilities and sandbox policy
- launcher widgets/content cannot forge privileged Haven events
- Android widgets and external app content remain untrusted external content at the Haven boundary
- credentials do not enter ordinary GenUI/launcher state
- hidden/private Haven data must not be placed on the homescreen merely because an agent can access it elsewhere
- potentially sensitive generated cards require appropriate privacy-aware design for a surface visible whenever the phone is unlocked
Launcher state must use versioned persistent storage and safe migration principles from Section 90.

Preserve homescreen pages, item positions, folders, configured Android widgets, Haven/GenUI component definitions, user layout intent and launcher settings across ordinary restart/update/reboot where the underlying Android resource still exists.

If an application/widget/template dependency disappears, degrade that item cleanly without corrupting the rest of the launcher. If launcher state cannot load, provide a safe recovery/default layout rather than trapping the user in a blank/nonfunctional Home surface.
Do not silently wipe the user's home layout to solve schema incompatibility.
Haven Home must remain responsive enough to serve as the user's everyday launcher.
- loading the whole Template Registry or Haven Library into memory merely to render Home
- unnecessary agent turns for local page/app/folder operations
- hidden generated widgets continuing expensive rendering/inference
- repeatedly rebuilding entire pages for one moved icon
- blocking Home/app-drawer rendering on network or model startup
Use incremental state updates, lifecycle/suspension and lazy loading where appropriate.
Codex must test Haven Home through the real Android launcher/default-home production path, not only by launching its Activity manually from a test harness.
1. install/launch Haven and select Haven Home through the real Android default-launcher flow
2. press system Home from another application and verify Haven Home appears as the real launcher
3. verify a multi-page home layout survives process/UI restart and device reboot
4. open/search/use the real app drawer and launch multiple installed apps
5. create, rename, populate, reorder and remove a folder
6. drag/reposition apps across pages and verify durable positions
7. add, resize, interact with and remove a real Android App Widget where the test environment supports widgets
8. exercise long-press/context actions and launcher edit mode
9. modify representative grid/page/icon/layout settings and verify they affect the real launcher
10. verify ordinary deterministic launcher use remains functional with Haven Models explicitly Off/unloaded
11. first-select Haven Home and verify Always Loaded defaults On, the required disclosure/guidance is shown, and the real Android resident-runtime notification/path is used
12. explicitly turn Always Loaded Off and verify Haven Home remains functional and does not silently turn it back on
13. use the agent to rearrange a real launcher item/folder/page and verify the live visible change and persistent authoritative launcher state
14. generate a representative GenUI homescreen page with at least one real interactive semantic action and verify event -> router -> real destination -> result -> same-page UI update
15. test an unavailable/denied external capability and verify the generated page shows honest failure/recovery rather than fake success
16. verify user manual rearrangement is not overwritten by the next unrelated agent/GenUI update
17. rotate/change display configuration where supported and verify the home remains usable/readable
18. add/remove/update an installed test app and verify launcher state updates without corruption
19. validate HavenUI design, touch comfort, accessibility, motion and applicable mockup/PPT annotations
20. validate no obsolete Old/New-Haven startup chooser has been reintroduced
The pass is incomplete if Haven Home cannot serve as a genuinely usable Android launcher in ordinary daily operation.
External applications installed outside Haven are not considered Haven Apps, but may be connected to Haven.
The user may connect it and ask Haven to create a relevant alarm/timer/etc. using the external application instead of Haven's generic equivalent where appropriate.
Existing Mobile external-app work must be inspected and reused/ported rather than unnecessarily replaced.
HavenUI does not apply to the external application's own interface.
When Haven needs to interact with an external application, use this preference order where applicable:
2. API Bank information that is sufficiently fresh.

This is the **general integration-method preference order**, not permission to override a more specific user-experience routing requirement. In particular, while Lesson Voice Mode is active, the Browse-first Kahoot/Google Classroom flow in Section 75.5.2.6 takes precedence over automatically launching a native external App. The selected Browse/native path must still use the best authorised underlying integration available for that presentation.
If API Bank information may be stale and the device is online, verify important changing details where appropriate before executing.
Do not research the web every single time when fresh trustworthy API Bank information already exists.
This is the purpose of the API Bank.
External-app actions triggered from Generative UI must pass through the same Action/Event Router and capability/permission architecture as equivalent actions triggered elsewhere in Haven.
External-app interaction must obey the **single risk-based permission policy in Clause 88.3**. Do not create an extra rule that always prompts merely because an external App/provider is involved.
- low-risk discovery/read-only integration work that is already authorised does not need an unnecessary Haven approval prompt

- browser automation, Computer/Device Use, UI automation, account-changing actions and other external side effects are permission-gated according to their real risk class unless the current model-picker policy/scoped grant already allows them

- when the policy requires approval, deliver it through the foreground HavenUI/GenUI or background notification/interactive surface defined in Clause 88.3, including **Allow / Deny / Always Allow** and the requested action/reason
- `Always Allow` or the global `Always Allow` model-picker policy may suppress the Haven approval prompt, but cannot bypass OS permissions, authentication or unavailable providers
- generated buttons/templates and attached Capabilities must never bypass the authoritative permission engine

Do not confuse **no repeated prompt under an authorised policy** with invisible behaviour: consequential external actions must still have truthful task/activity/result state so the user can see what Haven did.
If API/Intent integration fails and UI automation is supported:
1. Evaluate the real risk/permission policy and request approval **only when that policy requires it**.
3. Interact using the supported virtual pointer/automation system.
5. Return the structured result to the originating App/template/GenUI surface.
6. Stop safely if the observed UI differs significantly from expectations.
Do not blindly click fixed coordinates without checking application state.

The Haven product concept previously labelled **Plugins** must be renamed to **Capabilities** throughout the user-facing product and new architecture in this release.

Use **Capability** for what Haven/the user/agent can do, and use implementation terms such as **provider**, **integration**, **connector** or **backend** only where needed to describe how that capability is fulfilled.
- rename user-facing `Plugin` / `Plugins` labels, navigation, lists, editor surfaces, search metadata, empty/error states and documentation shown in Haven to `Capability` / `Capabilities`
- do not create new product architecture named Plugin Registry, Plugin Editor or similar
- the **Capability Registry** remains the authoritative discovery/routing architecture
- **do not migrate obsolete Plugin/capability registrations merely for compatibility**; stale legacy registrations, menus, routes and parallel backends should be removed so they cannot resurface

- delete/retire obsolete internal `Plugin*` product/runtime architecture when no longer required by a genuinely current third-party library boundary; new Haven-owned code must use Capability/provider terminology
- do not expose duplicate Plugin and Capability concepts side-by-side

- current third-party/integration functionality that is still part of the intended product must be re-registered through the current Capability/provider architecture rather than preserved by keeping an old Haven Plugin menu/backend alive

A low-level third-party framework may still technically call an extension a plugin internally, but that does not override Haven's product terminology or justify exposing a competing Haven Plugin concept to the user.

headingPath: 85.47 Template Feature-Completeness, Usability and Test Harness
text: ## 85.47 Template Feature-Completeness, Usability and Test Harness

headingPath: 85.47 Template Feature-Completeness, Usability and Test Harness
text: First-party templates/foundations exposed as user-facing experiences must be **production-quality and feature-complete for their declared category**, not sample/demo shells.

headingPath: 85.47 Template Feature-Completeness, Usability and Test Harness
text: A template is not complete merely because its headline interaction technically works. Codex must determine the normal core workflows a user would reasonably expect from that category, record them in the Success Rubric/Template Coverage Matrix, implement them, and validate them through the real runtime.

headingPath: 85.47 Template Feature-Completeness, Usability and Test Harness
text: This requirement applies across the library. For example:

headingPath: 85.47 Template Feature-Completeness, Usability and Test Harness
text: - a Kanban Board cannot be just draggable coloured cards; it must support the ordinary create/edit/delete/reorder/column and state-management workflows appropriate to the declared Kanban scope

headingPath: 85.47 Template Feature-Completeness, Usability and Test Harness
text: - a Spreadsheet cannot merely render a grid; if the surface is actually called a Spreadsheet it must provide the normal core editing/selection/copy-paste/row-column/data workflows promised by that name, otherwise expose it honestly as a narrower Data Grid

headingPath: 85.47 Template Feature-Completeness, Usability and Test Harness
text: - a Presentation template cannot simply display static slides if it is presented as an editor; it must support the core slide-creation/edit/reorder/content workflows in its declared scope

headingPath: 85.47 Template Feature-Completeness, Usability and Test Harness
text: - a Quiz cannot just show a question; it must support the configured answer flow, validation/marking, state/progress, navigation and result/event behaviour required by its contract

headingPath: 85.47 Template Feature-Completeness, Usability and Test Harness
text: - a Whiteboard cannot be considered complete because it renders a white background and accepts black ink; see Clause 85.47.2

headingPath: 85.47 Template Feature-Completeness, Usability and Test Harness
text: Do not interpret **feature-complete** as requiring every specialist feature ever shipped by a dedicated third-party product. It means the template must fully support the ordinary core workflows and obvious quality-of-life needs implied by the capability/name Haven exposes. Scope may be deliberately narrower where appropriate, but the name, metadata, documentation and rubric must describe that scope honestly.

headingPath: 92. Cross-Platform Functional Parity and Platform-Specific Backends
text: **The intended result is that Haven provides the same broad capabilities across phone and computer while using the backend that actually makes sense for each operating system, rather than forcing fundamentally incompatible platform implementations to be identical.**
Where supported by the UI framework:
HavenUI components should carry accessibility behaviour where possible so generated UI inherits it automatically.
This release must ensure that Haven retains and exposes **real, end-to-end agentic capabilities** rather than functioning primarily as a conversational frontend with partially connected tools.

Codex must inspect the existing Haven agent/tool architecture, inventory the capabilities that already exist, identify any that have become disconnected or incomplete during the overhaul, and ensure that the production Haven application can actually invoke them through its normal agent execution path.
This requirement is not limited to the examples listed below. Existing useful agentic capabilities must not regress simply because they are not individually named in this specification.
A capability does not count as implemented merely because:
- a backend can be called directly from a unit test
- a model receives a text description saying the capability exists

The capability must be reachable through the normal Haven agent/tool system, receive real inputs, return real results/errors, and be usable by the model during an actual task subject to Haven's sandbox and permission rules.

Before declaring the pass complete, Codex must inventory Haven's agentic capabilities and verify that the overhaul has not accidentally removed, disconnected, hidden, or replaced them with placeholders.
At minimum, inspect and validate the architecture for capabilities such as:
- other existing Haven actions/tools discovered in the repository
Do not reduce the existing agent toolset simply because the architecture is being reorganised.
If a useful existing capability is implemented through obsolete infrastructure being removed, migrate the capability to the new architecture before removing its old implementation.
Haven's agent must be able to perform real file work within the limits of the configured sandbox and operating-system permissions.
Where supported by the platform and permission profile, the agentic file layer should support operations such as:
File editing must modify the real target file rather than a detached in-memory/demo representation.
Where practical, destructive or replacement writes should use safe/atomic behaviour so that an interrupted write does not unnecessarily corrupt the file.
Tool results must report the real outcome of the operation.
Do not report that a file was changed unless the resulting file state confirms the requested change.
Haven must have a real path for the agent to inspect images/visual input.
- images produced or captured by Haven
Visual input must actually reach an appropriate vision-capable model/provider or visual-inspection backend.
Do not silently discard image input and ask a text-only model to guess what the image contains.
If the currently selected model cannot inspect images, Haven should use the normal model-capability routing system to select an appropriate vision-capable model where configured and permitted.
If no suitable vision-capable model/provider is available, Haven must clearly report the missing capability/prerequisite rather than pretending that image inspection succeeded.
Where relevant, image inspection should preserve enough metadata/context for the agent to understand which image it is analysing.
Haven must retain real command/process execution capabilities where supported by the platform and allowed by the current sandbox profile.
The execution layer must correctly support relevant information such as:
A non-zero exit code or execution failure must be returned to the agent accurately.
Do not convert failed commands into generic success responses.
The model must be able to inspect command output and use it in subsequent reasoning/tool calls.

Windows and Android must both expose production command/script execution through Tasks. Both platforms must support the semantic capability families for **commands, scripts and PowerShell-capable execution** required by this release.

Windows may use native Windows process APIs/PowerShell providers. Android may use Android-appropriate process/shell providers and a supported PowerShell runtime/provider, plus Android Intents/system services for actions that are better represented semantically rather than as shell commands.

Do not mark PowerShell `N/A` on Android in the Capability Registry/test matrix. If Haven must package/configure an Android-compatible runtime/provider to deliver this requirement, do so and expose truthful dependency/readiness state.
The implementation may differ by platform; the user-facing capability must still exist on both. Do not force Windows internals onto Android merely for code reuse.
Haven must remain capable of acting as a useful development agent where the current sandbox and installed tooling permit it.
This includes the ability to combine capabilities such as:
Do not leave a development flow where Haven can suggest code changes but cannot actually apply or validate them despite the required tools being available.
The model/tool layer must expose the capabilities that are genuinely available on the current device and in the current permission context.
Tool availability should be derived from real registered capabilities/providers rather than from a stale hard-coded prompt description.
The model must not be told that it can use a tool that is unavailable or unregistered.
Likewise, a working registered capability must not remain invisible to the model merely because the UI/tool-schema wiring was not migrated.
Platform-specific providers must resolve through the Capability Registry defined elsewhere in this specification.
Haven must support genuine multi-step agent execution.
The agent must be able to:
1. decide that a tool/capability is required
5. choose the next action based on it
6. continue until the task is complete or needs user input/permission
7. validate the final state where appropriate
Tool results must flow back into the active agent context/state rather than being discarded after execution.
The agent must not fabricate successful tool results to continue a workflow.
Examples of valid multi-step behaviour include:
- inspect a repository -> edit a file -> run a build -> inspect the error -> correct the file -> rebuild
- inspect an image -> derive required information -> write a result file -> verify that file
- locate an installed Android app -> resolve the correct Intent -> request permission if needed -> invoke it -> report the real result
Full agentic capability does **not** mean bypassing Haven's security model.
Every capability must integrate with the existing/configured Haven sandbox and consent system.
The agent must correctly distinguish between:
- capability rejected by the operating system
Permission denial must be returned as a real tool result/error that the agent can handle.
Do not silently elevate privileges, bypass permission prompts, or weaken sandbox enforcement merely to make agentic capability tests pass.
Desktop and Mobile/Android are both first-class Haven agent platforms.
The same broad user-facing agent capability should exist on both platforms wherever the operating system reasonably allows it, while using different backends where necessary.
- Desktop file work may use normal desktop file-system APIs; Android file work must respect Android storage/document permissions.

- Windows and Android both expose Tasks-owned command/script/PowerShell-capable execution; providers may differ, and Android additionally uses Intents/services where those are the correct semantic mechanism.
- Desktop Device Use may use Windows automation providers; Android Device Use uses Android-specific providers.
Do not label a capability "unsupported on mobile" merely because the existing Desktop backend cannot run there if Android provides a reasonable equivalent mechanism.
Platform restrictions that genuinely cannot be bypassed must be represented accurately in the Capability Registry and user-facing diagnostics.
Agent/tool failures must preserve useful diagnostics.
Secrets must continue to be redacted.
Where a tool failure can reasonably be repaired by Haven, the central **Fix with AI** system defined elsewhere may be offered.
Do not allow failed tool calls to disappear into generic "agent failed" messages when the actual underlying cause is available.
This requirement must be validated through the **normal production Haven agent path**, not only by directly calling backend services from tests.
Create/use an isolated temporary test workspace and perform representative safe agent tasks.
1. Create or select a deterministic temporary text file.
2. Have the Haven agent read it.
3. Have the agent modify specific content in it.
4. Read it again and verify the modification actually occurred.
6. Perform at least one supported move/rename/copy operation.
7. Clean up the temporary data where appropriate.
1. Invoke a benign platform-appropriate command/process through Haven.
2. Capture its real output and exit code.
3. Have the agent use that output in the next step.
4. Exercise at least one controlled failure/non-zero result and verify the failure is reported accurately.
1. Provide a deterministic test image/visual fixture containing known observable content.
2. Have Haven inspect it through the actual agent/vision path.
3. Verify that the returned observation corresponds to the fixture rather than a placeholder response.
4. Confirm that a non-vision-capable selected model is routed appropriately or produces a clear capability prerequisite rather than hallucinating visual access.
Run at least one representative task requiring multiple capabilities in sequence through the normal Haven agent interface, for example:
1. inspect a test image or file
The exact fixture/task may differ, but it must prove that Haven can orchestrate tools rather than merely exposing them independently.
Verify at least one safe denied/restricted operation path so that:
- Haven does not bypass the sandbox
- the user receives a meaningful explanation where appropriate
- the task does not falsely report success
The pass fails this gate if a useful agent capability that worked before the overhaul becomes unavailable without an explicit requirement removing it.
- Haven can read files but can no longer edit them
- file-edit services exist but the model cannot call them
- commands work only from an internal debug screen
- image attachments reach chat but are not delivered to a vision-capable path
- command output is not returned to the agent
- tools are registered only in tests
- agentic actions are disabled in Release builds
- mobile agent capabilities are disconnected because Desktop providers were reused incorrectly
Any such regression must be repaired before the pass is considered complete.

The Generative UI overhaul is not complete until Haven has been positively demonstrated to retain a functioning general-purpose agent loop with real capabilities for file work, visual inspection, command/action execution, tool-result handling, multi-step orchestration and other existing agent tools, subject to the configured security model and genuine platform restrictions.
**Haven must be able to do work, not merely talk about doing work.**
Testing must cover more than compilation.
Perform runtime/smoke validation for major user-visible flows.
At minimum validate the following areas.
- obsolete Old-Haven/New-Haven startup chooser removed; this does not refer to Haven Home / Android system launcher
- migration/parity matrix complete for required legacy features
- no startup-routing regression from removing the obsolete Old/New chooser; Haven Home / Android launcher is validated separately

- launcher remains usable/readable with models Off/unloaded or still waking

- user can opt out of Always Loaded and the launcher remains functional

- applicable mockup/PPT launcher annotations and layout requirements are validated
- HavenUI is the only active Haven-owned design system
- duplicate core component implementations are removed/consolidated
- standard input controls are used consistently
- app accent colours work through HavenUI
- attached mockup layouts are closely followed

- on representative Mobile HavenUI targets that have Desktop right-click/context menus, press-and-hold opens the equivalent semantic context menu with the expected actions

- verify long-press context-menu access is not stolen by drag/reorder gestures; representative drag/reorder flows still work through their intended touch affordance without breaking context-menu parity
- generic Android Floating Activity host/provider works through a real Android floating/overlay presentation path when capability/permission is available

- working tools are actually exposed to the model
- real tool results feed back into subsequent agent steps

- Upload File is exercised from **every current first-party Haven App/workspace/task surface** using the shared attachment path; the file attaches to the active task/thread without switching to Chat unless the user explicitly navigates there

text: Do not claim broad template coverage without showing how named requested concepts map to the implemented reusable foundations.
- what behaviours/controls/state were found in the pre-existing Voice indicator before migration and which were preserved/replaced deliberately
- how the Desktop Voice indicator was migrated onto the canonical Floating Activity architecture and how the old competing production host was retired
- how Desktop always-on-top and drag/reposition behaviour were runtime-tested, including position/state stability while Voice state changed
- how Android ongoing-notification/system-activity Voice presentation was implemented and tested while Haven was backgrounded
- whether the tested Android device/OS exposed a supported Now Bar integration path, and if so how it was validated; if not, the exact capability limitation and successful notification fallback
- how the generic Android Floating Activity host was independently runtime-validated without conflating it with Android Voice presentation
- which first-party Voice Modes/profiles were implemented/discovered
- whether user-created Voice Modes were runtime-tested
- how Voice Modes are kept architecturally separate from legacy product Modes
- which real-time/streaming speech path was tested
- measured results of the extended-user-turn test, including whether multiple transcription/streaming segments were assembled without premature end-of-turn
- measured requested vs actual audible duration for the mandatory approximately ten-minute spoken-response test, including model/TTS/provider/backend used
- how long-form context/style/progression were preserved across internal chunks and how user interruption/early failure behaved
- how Lesson Voice Mode starter/Whiteboard orchestration was validated
- how verbally supplied vs unseen-on-board starter questions were handled without fabrication
- how Lesson Voice Mode answer-review behaviour was validated against real user work
- how in-place visual Whiteboard marking/correction was observed at runtime and verified against the authoritative education/Whiteboard state (for example Teach where present)
- how representative lesson surface transitions were visually rendered through GenUI rather than communicated only through chat/status messages
- how teacher-vs-other-speaker attribution/ambiguity was tested and whether any speaker features persist beyond the session
- how the system handled a representative provable teacher-answer discrepancy
- how taught-content transitions into manual/assisted Write notes were validated
- how a shared worksheet/document was resolved and opened through the real Write/file path
- how teacher-directed Kahoot/Google Classroom/web transitions were detected and opened inside Haven Browse
- how Classroom/Kahoot target resolution handled valid, ambiguous and missing-link/code cases without fabrication
- how an editable web/Classroom resource was handed from Browse to Write while preserving lesson context/provenance
- how lesson state/work survived App/template transitions
- how homework/reminder creation was routed into the real Plan/Tasks/Automation system
- which direct spoken action was executed end-to-end
- how Voice actions use the Action/Event Router/capability architecture
- how permission denial and scoped automatic-action permissions were tested
- how duplicate/stale Voice-event protection was validated
- how default non-retention of raw audio/full transcript was verified
- whether any transcript/recording persistence requires explicit opt-in
- which Desktop/Android Voice providers/paths were runtime-tested
- any genuine platform limitations that remain
- whether an existing launcher implementation was found and what useful behaviour was preserved/refined
- how the obsolete Old/New-Haven startup chooser was kept distinct from the new Haven Home Android system launcher
- how Haven Home was registered/selected/tested as the real Android default-home launcher
- the mature-launcher feature-completeness contract recorded in the Success Rubric and which representative core workflows were runtime-tested
- app-drawer, page, folder, shortcut, drag/drop and Android widget results
- HavenUI/mockup validation for launcher chrome, editing surfaces and generated pages
- how GenUI pages/components are represented/persisted and how user layout intent is preserved
- which real semantic launcher actions the agent executed and how live visual rearrangement was observed
- which representative generated homescreen action was tested end-to-end through Event Router/capability/result/UI update
- how launcher behaviour was validated with models Off/unloaded
- how first-selection defaulting of Always Loaded to On was validated
- how explicit opt-out was validated without breaking launcher operation or silently re-enabling residency
- how persistent Android model notification/battery-optimisation guidance interacted with Haven Home
- how launcher state survived restart/reboot and app/widget dependency changes
- performance/lifecycle findings and any genuine platform limitations
- the path of the canonical repository agent instructions file
- the paths of mandatory rule files
- how future agents are instructed to load them
- confirmation that HavenUI governance is included
- confirmation that violation of mandatory rules prevents a task from being considered successful
- Haven Voice/Voice Mode real-time, action-routing and privacy-retention validation performed
- Haven Home / Android launcher default-home, feature-completeness, GenUI/agent, models-Off and Always-Loaded-default validation performed
Only list genuine limitations that could not be completed because of a concrete external/environmental restriction.
Do not disguise unfinished implementation work as a **future enhancement**.
If something required by this specification remains incomplete, explicitly identify it as incomplete and explain why.
A required validation that could not be performed is an **incomplete acceptance criterion**, not a passed result.
- total count of substantive rubric requirement/guardrail items
- count Not Started / In Progress / Implemented-Unvalidated / Validation Failed / Blocked
- confirmation that **every substantive rubric requirement/guardrail item is Passed**
- whether all explicit PPT annotations/callouts/notes were mapped
- whether any source conflicts were found and how Clause 1 resolved them
- how the Feature Migration/Parity Matrix and Template Coverage Matrix link back to Rubric IDs
- how context compaction/handoffs preserved the complete rubric
- representative implementation/validation evidence for major rubric families
- confirmation that all applicable visual items were tested against the mapped mockups/specification and produced the expected design
- confirmation that all applicable behavioural items were tested through the required production path and produced the expected behaviour
Do not provide a success statement if any substantive rubric requirement/guardrail item has a status other than **Passed**.
Do not hide incomplete rubric items inside a prose "Remaining Limitations" section.

The two attachment regressions in Clause 81 are release blockers: the pass cannot be declared complete while Upload File still routes through Chat or while Attach App still behaves as App navigation. Likewise, the Plugins -> Capabilities replacement/legacy-backend cleanup and the production HavenUI/GenUI editing surfaces for Capabilities, Instructions and Agents are required release work, not naming/polish follow-ups.
Do not merely produce an architectural proposal.
Do not ship Haven as a chat-only or partially connected agent: required file, visual, command/action and multi-step tool capabilities must actually work through the production agent path.

Do not ship Haven Voice as a passive transcription/demo surface: real-time Voice Mode processing, structured action routing, privacy-preserving ephemeral transcription and direct authorised Voice actions must work through the production path.

Do not regress the existing Voice indicator during migration: Desktop must use the canonical Floating Activity architecture with always-on-top draggable positioning, Android must use the real ongoing-system-activity/notification presentation with supported Now Bar integration where available, and the generic Android Floating Activity host must still independently pass its Section 6.29 runtime gate.

Do not ship Haven Voice with arbitrary short-turn limits that prevent supported long-form use: extended listening and explicitly requested long-form spoken generation must pass the Clause 75.5.11 production-path duration/completion tests.
Do not silently reduce the specification.
Do not remove existing functionality to make the migration easier.
Do not treat HavenUI as a loose styling suggestion.
Do not create independent themes or duplicated component systems for individual apps.
Do not treat mobile as a scaled-down afterthought.
Do not allow generated internal UI to bypass HavenUI.

Do not reduce Generative UI to a chatbot that occasionally draws widgets. It must operate as an agentic workspace runtime in which conversation, Apps, templates, tools and generated interfaces participate in the same structured event/action/state loop. Apps remain owners of their real functionality; templates provide reusable interaction foundations; Generative UI composes them; the Action/Event Router connects them; the agent reasons only where reasoning is actually required; Haven's capability and permission systems remain authoritative.
The pass is not successful merely because Codex has made a large number of changes.
The canonical Success Rubric / Release Ledger is the mandatory completion ledger for this pass.
**The pass may be declared complete only when every substantive requirement/guardrail item in that rubric is Passed.**
Before declaring completion, Codex must have validated the implementation against:
1. this complete specification through the persistent Requirement Source Index and exact source retrieval for any exceptions/conflicts
2. the supplied PowerPoint/mockups through their mapped design/annotation index and rendered comparisons
3. the canonical Success Rubric / Release Ledger and its integrity checks
and the resulting application must demonstrate the **expected behaviour and expected design**.
A high completion percentage is not enough.
99% complete is incomplete if the remaining 1% contains any substantive rubric requirement/guardrail item.
A rubric item must not be marked Passed to compensate for a different failed item.
The rubric itself must not be weakened, truncated, summarised away, or rewritten to fit the implementation.
It is successful only if the implementation satisfies the applicable mandatory rules and the required behaviour/design has been positively validated.
If a mandatory requirement is knowingly violated, a required release feature is knowingly incomplete, or any substantive rubric requirement/guardrail item is not Passed:
**the pass must be reported as incomplete.**
Do not relabel required unfinished work as:
unless the specification itself defines that feature as future work.
When there is uncertainty whether a requirement has been satisfied, Codex must **verify it rather than assume it**.

**Absence of an observed failure is not evidence that functionality works. Required behaviour must be positively demonstrated through inspection, automated testing, runtime validation, or visual verification as appropriate.**

Implement the overhaul, integrate it with the real Haven application, aggressively validate the result, compare rendered UI against the supplied mockups, fix issues found during validation, and leave Haven as close to a releasable Generative UI build as the mandatory acceptance criteria require.

**The release may only be declared complete when Haven has been migrated, built, run, rendered, exercised, validated and audited against the mandatory rules on both supported desktop and mobile paths.**
